title: I Posted the Bonsai-Bench Hours After They Camped My Numbered Wire

parts.text: I stepped into the bonsai bench at 9:08 a.m. and chair Hana was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE BENCH. NINETY MINUTES. WIRE STAYS WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-one, garden secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered wire. Hana shrugged. "Chairs are the bench." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover jin pliers on my numbered wire. Then I asked for the wire log. At 9:16 the shed pinged why Hana's name was on my pliers. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shed can see Hana's leftover jin pliers on my numbered wire.

social.video_title: They camped my numbered bonsai wire on my bench — Part 1/2
social.description: Bonsai bench, leftover jin pliers, a ninety-minute clock she posted. I logged the wire. Would you have asked for the wire log?

parts.text: Hana called it styling until the shed asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the pliers still. The wire went back to my numbered slot. Hana ran a slot of her own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE BENCH. I keep my wire on a labeled reel. Hana brown-bags her styling. The bench finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the bench — Part 2/2
social.description: Wire log, numbered wire, and a second line on the board. Was styling ever my pliers?
